title: The right to repair
voice: Every title, desc, comment or intro here is read by a player and is written as Envie speaking. See CLAUDE.md and _DESIGNS/envie-voice-and-text-rewrite-guide.md: plain short sentences, no em-dashes, European spelling, no emoji, facts and sources untouched. The optional 'envie' line on a slide is his own aside, one short sentence.

slides.text: Your washing machine breaks. The engineer says a new one is cheaper.
slides.footer: I heard that sentence twice in one week here. So I went looking into why.

slides.text: Here is what I found. People did not stop fixing things because they stopped caring. Fixing things was quietly made awkward.
slides.footer: Spare parts priced like gold. Manuals kept in-house. Software that refuses a part it did not come with.
slides.envie: That last one still annoys me.

slides.footer: Broken electronics are the fastest growing pile of rubbish on the planet.

slides.caption: That is how much waste each person in Ireland throws out in a year. Sixth highest in the EU. A fair bit of it still worked on the way to the bin.
slides.bold: still worked on the way to the bin
slides.envie: I did not expect that from a country this green.

slides.text: So people started asking for something simple. The right to get their own things fixed.
slides.bold: The right to get their own things fixed.

slides.text: Last summer they got it. New EU rules say that if a thing can be fixed, the maker has to fix it when you ask.
slides.bold: the maker has to fix it when you ask
slides.footer: Free or at a fair price, and reasonably quickly. Even after your guarantee has run out.
slides.envie: Fair play to whoever pushed for that.

slides.text: And it is not some obscure list. It is the stuff in your kitchen and your pocket.
slides.envie: I checked for the hoover. It is on there.

slides.title: What changes when something breaks
bad: A part that cost more than the machine
A quote that moved every time you rang
Software blocking a part that was not theirs
good: Parts priced so repair makes sense
A written quote that holds for 30 days
No blocking a repair without a real reason

slides.text: There is a small bonus too. Pick the repair instead of the replacement and you get an extra year of guarantee on top.
slides.footer: Doing the better thing no longer costs you your cover.
slides.envie: Maith thú to whoever thought of that bit.

slides.text: Every device in your house is a tiny mine. Metals dug up, shipped, refined, then glued together tight.
slides.footer: From up there I watched the holes in the ground getting bigger. You would want to keep this stuff in use.

slides.text: Which is why fixing things is the quiet heart of the circular economy. Not recycling. Recycling is the last resort, for when everything else has failed.
slides.bold: the quiet heart of the circular economy
slides.footer: Ireland has been good at collecting broken electronics for twenty years. It has just been counting tonnes recycled, rather than things kept alive.
slides.envie: Odd, that. The better outcome counts for less.

slides.text: Search for someone to fix it, not something to replace it.
slides.footer: That is the whole shift, really.

slides.text: So next time something packs in, look up who near you can fix it before you look up what to replace it with.
slides.bold: who near you can fix it
slides.footer: RepairMyStuff.ie is free, run by Monaghan County Council with the EPA, and it is now Ireland's official national repair platform. Search your county, pick your category, phones to fridges to furniture.
slides.envie: Go on then. I will be trying it myself.
